title: What If Antarctica Were Covered in Forest? It Once Was

scenes.text: What if Antarctica was covered in forest? Over 260 million years ago, it was.
Geologists found fossil trees on the McIntyre Promontory, in the Transantarctic Mountains.
Back then Antarctica was warmer and more humid, and the forest grew with mosses and ferns.
Tree rings show the trees went from summer growth to winter dormancy in about a month.
The forest may have stretched across the supercontinent Gondwana.
Then, 251 million years ago, a mass extinction wiped out over 90 percent of species, polar forests included.
